budget_items.what_was_said: The director read out the town's FY27 allocation for programs, MOC, training, office supplies and mileage, noting it does not include salaries.
A board member asked to see FY26 actual spending for the department; the director said the town has not closed out FY26 yet and may have until September.

A board member noted the outreach coordinator position was unfilled for part of the year, leaving unspent salary money, and suggested transferring leftover funds within the department before it reverts to general fund.

budget_items.topic: Transfer from salary to office supplies (FY26, already done)
budget_items.what_was_said: The director confirmed a transfer was already made from the salary line to help cover office supplies this year, though could not state the exact amount.
The director said the COA gift fund currently holds a small balance and has not been spent, and that no written procedure exists for how the board may authorize its use.
A board member asked whether furniture had come out of the gift fund; the director clarified it came from a grant instead.

budget_items.topic: MOC (Monus Opportunity Council / Meals on Wheels) donation
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member explained MOC is an annual donation the COA makes, associated with Meals on Wheels.

budget_items.topic: Senior means-tested real estate tax exemption
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member said qualifying could mean a tax exemption, and combined with the circuit breaker credit (if also qualified) could total a larger reduction, with a filing deadline of September 2nd.

budget_items.topic: Elderly exemption and circuit breaker combined relief
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member said the separate elderly exemption is worth a set amount on its own, and combined with the circuit breaker could total up to a larger figure in relief.

transfers.description: Salary line (unfilled outreach coordinator position) to office supplies line, within COA department, FY26

what_happened.line: The board asked the director to draft a written policy for the COA gift fund, which currently has no procedure governing how it can be spent.
The FY27 department budget was read aloud, covering programs, training and supplies, but the figure does not include salaries.
Members noted the outreach coordinator position sat vacant for part of the year, and a transfer from that salary line to office supplies had already been made.
The board urged seniors to file for the means-tested tax exemption and circuit breaker credit before the deadline.
Funding for the September honorary-member luncheon was left to the director's discretion, with the board leaning toward voluntary member contributions rather than a program or meal account.

why_it_matters: The gift fund is money donated to the Council on Aging, and the absence of a written approval procedure means there is currently no documented rule for how the board authorizes its use.
Seniors who qualify can combine the elderly exemption and the circuit breaker credit to reduce a property tax bill, but only if they file by the deadline the board flagged.
Moving unspent salary money to cover office supplies is a within-department transfer the board discussed doing again before any leftover FY26 funds revert to the town's general fund.
